id: c-graph-toolkit
title: Graph Toolkit: BFS, Topological Order, Components, Dijkstra
difficulty: Hard
order: 1
tags: graphs, CSR, BFS, topological sort, union-find, Dijkstra
time_limit: 2
---
## Statement
Load a **directed weighted graph** into CSR arrays and answer several classic questions about it.

Input: `V E`, then E lines `u v w` (0 ≤ u, v < V, 1 ≤ w ≤ 1000, directed edge u→v with weight w; parallel edges and self-loops are possible), then queries:

| Query | Output |
|---|---|
| `bfs S` | `bfs S: reached R, farthest D (vertex X)`: hop distances ignoring weights; X is the smallest-numbered vertex at the maximum distance |
| `topo` | `topo: a b c ...` (Kahn's algorithm, always taking the **smallest available** vertex: use a min-heap), or `topo: cycle`. When V > 20, print only the first 10 vertices followed by ` ... (V vertices)` |
| `wcc` | `wcc: N components, largest L`: weakly connected components (ignore direction), using union-find |
| `dijkstra S T` | `dijkstra S->T: cost C, path S ... T` (with ties among equal-cost paths broken by preferring the smaller predecessor), or `unreachable` |

V is up to 100 000 and E up to 300 000.

## Starter
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main(void) {
    return 0;
}
```

## Hints
- CSR: count out-degrees into `start[u + 1]`, take prefix sums, then fill `adj[]` and `wt[]` using a copy of `start` as write cursors.
- BFS with an array queue. Distances are initialised to -1.
- Topological order with the smallest vertex first: Kahn's algorithm with a **min-heap** of zero in-degree vertices instead of a FIFO queue. If fewer than V vertices come out, there's a cycle.
- Union-find with path compression over the edges, ignoring direction.
- Dijkstra with a binary heap of `(dist, vertex)`, lazy deletion, and `long long` distances. Tie-break: when `nd == dist[v]` and `u < pred[v]`, update `pred[v]`. Reconstruct the path by following `pred` backwards from T.


## Solution
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

typedef struct { long long d; int v; } HItem;

static void h_push(HItem *h, int *n, HItem x) {
    int i = (*n)++;
    h[i] = x;
    while (i > 0) {
        int p = (i - 1) / 2;
        if (h[p].d < h[i].d || (h[p].d == h[i].d && h[p].v <= h[i].v)) break;
        HItem t = h[p]; h[p] = h[i]; h[i] = t;
        i = p;
    }
}
static HItem h_pop(HItem *h, int *n) {
    HItem top = h[0];
    h[0] = h[--(*n)];
    int i = 0;
    for (;;) {
        int l = 2 * i + 1, r = l + 1, m = i;
        if (l < *n && (h[l].d < h[m].d || (h[l].d == h[m].d && h[l].v < h[m].v))) m = l;
        if (r < *n && (h[r].d < h[m].d || (h[r].d == h[m].d && h[r].v < h[m].v))) m = r;
        if (m == i) break;
        HItem t = h[i]; h[i] = h[m]; h[m] = t;
        i = m;
    }
    return top;
}

static int find(int *par, int x) {
    while (par[x] != x) { par[x] = par[par[x]]; x = par[x]; }
    return x;
}

int main(void) {
    int V, E;
    if (scanf("%d %d", &V, &E) != 2) return 1;
    int *eu = malloc((size_t)(E + 1) * sizeof(int)), *ev = malloc((size_t)(E + 1) * sizeof(int)), *ew = malloc((size_t)(E + 1) * sizeof(int));
    int *start = calloc((size_t)V + 1, sizeof(int)), *adj = malloc((size_t)(E + 1) * sizeof(int)), *wt = malloc((size_t)(E + 1) * sizeof(int));
    for (int i = 0; i < E; i++) { scanf("%d %d %d", &eu[i], &ev[i], &ew[i]); start[eu[i] + 1]++; }
    for (int v = 0; v < V; v++) start[v + 1] += start[v];
    int *cur = malloc((size_t)V * sizeof(int));
    memcpy(cur, start, (size_t)V * sizeof(int));
    for (int i = 0; i < E; i++) { adj[cur[eu[i]]] = ev[i]; wt[cur[eu[i]]++] = ew[i]; }

    int *dist = malloc((size_t)V * sizeof(int)), *queue = malloc((size_t)V * sizeof(int));
    HItem *heap = malloc((size_t)(E + V + 1) * sizeof(HItem));
    char cmd[16];
    while (scanf("%15s", cmd) == 1) {
        if (!strcmp(cmd, "bfs")) {
            int s; scanf("%d", &s);
            for (int v = 0; v < V; v++) dist[v] = -1;
            int head = 0, tail = 0, reached = 0, far = s;
            dist[s] = 0; queue[tail++] = s;
            while (head < tail) {
                int u = queue[head++];
                reached++;
                if (dist[u] > dist[far] || (dist[u] == dist[far] && u < far)) far = u;
                for (int k = start[u]; k < start[u + 1]; k++)
                    if (dist[adj[k]] == -1) { dist[adj[k]] = dist[u] + 1; queue[tail++] = adj[k]; }
            }
            printf("bfs %d: reached %d, farthest %d (vertex %d)\n", s, reached, dist[far], far);
        } else if (!strcmp(cmd, "topo")) {
            int *indeg = calloc((size_t)V, sizeof(int)), n = 0, out = 0;
            for (int i = 0; i < E; i++) indeg[ev[i]]++;
            for (int v = 0; v < V; v++) if (!indeg[v]) h_push(heap, &n, (HItem){v, v});
            int *order = malloc((size_t)V * sizeof(int));
            while (n) {
                int u = h_pop(heap, &n).v;
                order[out++] = u;
                for (int k = start[u]; k < start[u + 1]; k++)
                    if (--indeg[adj[k]] == 0) h_push(heap, &n, (HItem){adj[k], adj[k]});
            }
            if (out < V) printf("topo: cycle\n");
            else {
                printf("topo:");
                for (int i = 0; i < (V <= 20 ? V : 10); i++) printf(" %d", order[i]);
                if (V > 20) printf(" ... (%d vertices)", V);
                printf("\n");
            }
            free(indeg); free(order);
        } else if (!strcmp(cmd, "wcc")) {
            int *par = malloc((size_t)V * sizeof(int)), *cnt = calloc((size_t)V, sizeof(int));
            for (int v = 0; v < V; v++) par[v] = v;
            for (int i = 0; i < E; i++) {
                int a = find(par, eu[i]), b = find(par, ev[i]);
                if (a != b) par[a] = b;
            }
            int comps = 0, largest = 0;
            for (int v = 0; v < V; v++) { int r = find(par, v); if (cnt[r]++ == 0) comps++; if (cnt[r] > largest) largest = cnt[r]; }
            printf("wcc: %d components, largest %d\n", comps, largest);
            free(par); free(cnt);
        } else if (!strcmp(cmd, "dijkstra")) {
            int s, t; scanf("%d %d", &s, &t);
            long long *d = malloc((size_t)V * sizeof(long long));
            int *pred = malloc((size_t)V * sizeof(int)), n = 0;
            for (int v = 0; v < V; v++) { d[v] = -1; pred[v] = -1; }
            d[s] = 0;
            h_push(heap, &n, (HItem){0, s});
            while (n) {
                HItem it = h_pop(heap, &n);
                if (it.d != d[it.v]) continue;                    /* stale entry */
                int u = it.v;
                for (int k = start[u]; k < start[u + 1]; k++) {
                    int v = adj[k];
                    long long nd = d[u] + wt[k];
                    if (d[v] == -1 || nd < d[v]) { d[v] = nd; pred[v] = u; h_push(heap, &n, (HItem){nd, v}); }
                    else if (nd == d[v] && v != s && u < pred[v]) pred[v] = u;
                }
            }
            if (d[t] == -1) printf("dijkstra %d->%d: unreachable\n", s, t);
            else {
                int *path = malloc((size_t)V * sizeof(int)), len = 0;
                for (int v = t; v != -1 && len < V; v = (v == s ? -1 : pred[v])) path[len++] = v;
                printf("dijkstra %d->%d: cost %lld, path", s, t, d[t]);
                for (int i = len - 1; i >= 0; i--) printf(" %d", path[i]);
                printf("\n");
                free(path);
            }
            free(d); free(pred);
        }
    }
    return 0;
}
```

- **CSR (compressed sparse row)** stores all adjacency lists in two flat arrays: one allocation, sequential memory, O(V + E) space. That's how high-performance graph libraries and sparse matrices store graphs.
- **BFS** gives hop distances in O(V + E). **Kahn's algorithm with a min-heap** gives the lexicographically smallest topological order, or detects a cycle when some vertices never reach in-degree 0.
- **Union-find** with path halving answers connectivity in near-constant amortised time per edge.
- **Dijkstra with lazy deletion** skips stale heap entries instead of using decrease-key, in O((V + E) log V). The deterministic tie-break on predecessors makes the reported path unique.
